thread:
leah.sales: Client POC hit a hard failure when they POST the whole conversation with screenshots: client sees a 413 and the assistant later "loses" the system prompt. They want an explanation and a workaround.

omar.eng: Do we have gateway + runtime lines?

leah.sales: Gateway shows `gateway-us-west: client=203.0.113.7 request="POST /v1/chat" content_length=3710456 status=413`. Runtime shows a separate event: `runtime: reject request, reason=sequence_length 19840 > max_input_tokens 16384 org=org_T9`. So two different limits triggered across retries.

jenna-sre: Exactly  gateway HTTP body limit (default ~2MB) returns 413; if the gateway accepts a large body it can still be rejected by runtime on sequence length with a 400. Their client retried and eventually hit both.

paul-ps: They embedded images as base64 and also include long system + user turns. Short-term we should advise: (1) Use presigned URLs (short TTL) or our upload API instead of inline base64. (2) Enable `Content-Encoding: gzip` on the request header. (3) Switch to a multipart/form-data upload: upload files first, then send a small JSON body referencing the file ids or URLs.

omar.eng: Adding technical detail for the client: our gateway accepts compressed payloads if header `Content-Encoding: gzip` is present; many chat histories compress 70-90% and drop under the 2MB limit. For attachments, multipart upload reduces memory spike because body parts are streamed and the gateway enforces per-part buffering.

leah.sales: Customer asked if multipart avoids the sequence-length check at runtime.

jenna-sre: No. Multipart reduces HTTP body size and memory pressure but it doesn't change token counting. Sequence length is calculated from the reconstructed message tokens inside the runtime. You still need to cap tokens via `max_input_tokens` or truncate histories.

paul-ps: Practical template to share with developers (copy-paste):
```
1) Upload attachments via presigned URL or /v1/files endpoint; get back file_id or url.
2) Build chat payload referencing file_id(s); keep message text only in the JSON body.
3) Add header: `Content-Encoding: gzip` when sending the JSON payload.
4) SDK options: set `truncate: "tail"` and `max_input_tokens: 8192`.
```

omar.eng: For POC escalation: we can provision a short-lived sandbox with a higher gateway body limit (6MB) and a dedicated runtime bumped to 32k tokens for org_T9, but that requires an ops ticket, SRE review, and an org-level trial agreement. Request will include a guardrail: runtime will still enforce `max_input_tokens` configurable per-org so we won't OOM.

leah.sales: Customer is willing to sign a trial addendum. Can ops do the short-lived bump while we iterate on the JS client?

jenna-sre: ops-bot: ticket #3021 created for gateway + runtime bump for org_T9, status: awaiting-approval :rotating_light: (SRE to review memory/cost risk).

paul-ps: Also advise: if they insist on sending full raw history continually, run a rolling summarizer on the client to compress older turns and include a checksum or version token so the runtime can rehydrate context if needed. That avoids sending megabytes of raw tokens every request.

leah.sales: Can you draft a short email with the multipart + presigned URL example, and a line about pricing impact so I can share with procurement?

paul-ps: Sent. Pricing note included: increasing sequence cap increases potential tokens per-call; we estimated worst-case delta and added it to the email.

leah.sales: Thanks all. Action items: paul to share code samples (done), jenna to follow ops ticket #3021, omar to help client test gzip + multipart tomorrow morning.
